title: Marginal likelihoods, Bayes factors, and empirical Bayes

items.title: Expected mean squares in the balanced one-way normal random-effects model
items.statement: For k,r>=2 and the independent balanced model Y_ij=mu+a_i+epsilon_ij with a_i~N(0,tau^2), epsilon_ij~N(0,sigma^2), tau^2>=0, sigma^2>0, the between and within mean squares have expectations sigma^2+r tau^2 and sigma^2. Equating these moments gives the raw method-of-moments estimate (MSB-MSW)/r.
items.axiom_use: AC is required by the library's normal-law definition and its normal-moment supplier. The expectation and variance algebra uses no additional choice.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §5.4
NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, §7.4.4, What are variance components?

items.title: Marginal likelihoods, proper model evidence, and Bayes factors
items.statement: For each of finitely many models with a proper parameter prior and a specified jointly measurable likelihood density f_i(theta,y) against one common sigma-finite data measure mu, define m_i(y)=integral f_i(theta,y) Pi_i(d theta). This is the prior-predictive density, or marginal likelihood/evidence. For two models i and j with positive finite evidences define BF_ji(y)=m_j(y)/m_i(y); arbitrary model prior weights w_i>0 summing to one define prior odds w_j/w_i.
items.axiom_use: None beyond the axioms already declared by the cited measure and density interfaces.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §7.4
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8, §§8.2.1–8.2.2

items.title: Finite-model posterior probabilities and Bayes-factor odds
items.statement: Under the finite dominated model setup of def-marginal-likelihood-and-bayes-factor, if every model weight is positive and every model evidence at y is finite and positive, then the model-index posterior has version P(M=i|y)=w_i m_i(y)/sum_j w_j m_j(y). For any two models j,i its posterior odds are prior odds times BF_ji=m_j(y)/m_i(y).
items.axiom_use: None. The finite disjoint-union construction and the dominated-kernel Bayes formula are choice-free.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §7.4
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8, §8.2.1

items.title: Type-II maximum marginal likelihood and empirical-Bayes plug-in posterior
items.statement: In a finite-group hierarchy with conditional parameter kernel G_eta and specified jointly measurable likelihood density, define m(y|eta) by integrating the conditional likelihood over G_eta^tensor m. Define a Type-II maximum-marginal-likelihood choice only at data y where eta->m(y|eta) is finite-valued and attains a positive finite maximum; a data-indexed rule requires a measurable maximizing selection. Its plug-in posterior is the normalized conditional update at that selected eta. Full Bayes retains the posterior distribution of eta and may induce group dependence after eta is integrated out; no generic empirical-Bayes risk, consistency, dominance, or coverage guarantee is asserted.
items.axiom_use: No new axiom is asserted. The referenced hierarchical posterior theorem carries only its stated hypotheses.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §§5.1, 5.3–5.4
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 16, §§16.3–16.4

title: Marginal likelihoods, Bayes factors, and empirical Bayes — Examples

items.title: A negative balanced-ANOVA moment estimate
items.statement: With k=r=2 and observations (-1,1) in both groups, MSB=0, MSW=2, and the raw moment estimate of tau^2 is -1. Under positive tau^2 and sigma^2 this occurs on a positive-probability neighborhood, so truncating at zero changes the estimator and does not prove a structural zero.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the library's normal-law and normal-density suppliers; no additional choice is used.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §5.4

items.title: A diffuse normal prior changes the point-null Bayes factor
items.statement: Compare a point-null model theta=0 with a normal alternative theta~N(0,tau^2), Y|theta~N(theta,sigma^2), sigma^2>0. At fixed y=0 the alternative-to-null Bayes factor is sqrt(sigma^2/(sigma^2+tau^2)), which tends to zero as the alternative prior variance grows.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the library normal-law and density suppliers; the Gaussian integral calculation uses no additional choice.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §7.4
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8, §8.2.2

items.title: An improper flat-prior scale makes a formal evidence arbitrary
items.statement: For one normal location observation with known positive variance, the likelihood integral against c times Lebesgue measure equals c. Two model-specific improper flat priors therefore give a formal evidence ratio c_2/c_1 that changes with arbitrary scales, so it is not a Bayes factor defined by the proper-prior model evidence.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the normal-density supplier and implies Countable Choice for the Lebesgue sigma-finiteness and interval-volume facts. No additional choice is used.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §7.4

items.title: A shared hyperparameter can couple group parameters
items.statement: Let eta be uniform on {0,1}, let theta_1,theta_2 be conditionally independent with theta_j=eta, and let the singleton observations carry no information. The full posterior leaves the shared eta uncertain and makes theta_1,theta_2 dependent; Type-II plug-in at eta=0 gives a different posterior.
items.axiom_use: None. The finite hierarchy, posterior normalization, and calculations use no choice axiom.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §§5.1, 5.3–5.4
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 16, §§16.3–16.4

items.title: A point-null hypothesis needs a model atom
items.statement:
Let $M_0$ have parameter space $\Theta_0=\{0\}$ and prior $\Pi_0=\delta_0$,
and let $M_1$ have parameter space $\Theta_1=[0,1]$ and uniform prior
$\Pi_1=\lambda|_{[0,1]}$. Use the common data space $\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}$ with
counting measure $\mu$, and specify the jointly measurable Bernoulli density
on each parameter space by $f_i(\theta,0)=1-\theta$ and
$f_i(\theta,1)=\theta$. Give the models prior weights $w_0,w_1>0$ with
$w_0+w_1=1$. After observing $y=0$, model $M_0$ has positive posterior
probability because it is an explicit model atom with positive prior weight. A
single continuous prior on $[0,1]$ instead assigns $\theta=0$ probability
zero.
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used only through the stated Lebesgue-volume supplier; the finite-model calculation is choice-free.

references.title: Andrew Gelman et al., Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd ed., §7.4
Alicia A. Johnson, Miles Q. Ott, and Mine Dogucu, Bayes Rules!, Chapter 8, §8.2.2
